title: Park's Three Phases
welcome_lead: Trace recovery from impact to reconstruction.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on Park's model, recovery phases and case applications.
final_note: Quality of life curves can exceed pre-event levels.

concepts.def: Quality of life baseline; preparation level varies.
Event causes sharp drop; deaths, damage.
Months-years: rebuild infrastructure better than before.
Depends on aid speed, governance, capital, preparation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Park (1991) proposed a 3-phase model. Quality of life axis (y) vs time (x). Sharp drop at impact; gradual recovery thereafter. Curve can return below, to, or above pre-event level. Steepness of recovery reflects governance capacity and external aid.

Mw 9.0 + tsunami killed 18500; displaced 470000. JSDF mobilised 100000 personnel within 24 hours. Reconstruction budget ~£200 billion. Coastal sea walls rebuilt to 15 m. By 2021 most areas above pre-event quality of life via build-back-better policy.

Mw 7.8 (April) killed 9000; damaged 800000 homes. Six months later 70 percent still in temporary shelter; political deadlock delayed funds. By 2023 only 75 percent of homes rebuilt; many to original standards. Highlights how governance constrains Park's curve.
